messages:
Liz (Support): Hey team — customer reported intermittent failures on the embeddings endpoint and we think it ties to batching behavior. They see a lot of 400s with "dimension mismatch" and occasional tail latency spikes when their QPS bursts. Full customer note pasted below and I attached their minimal repro. Can we triage?

Customer notes: 
- endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings
- model: embed-redwood-1 (they assume 1536 dims)
- error: 400 "embedding dim mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024"
- observed tail latency: p99 spikes from 120ms -> 1.2s during bursts

Repro (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"embed-redwood-1","input":["hello world","foo bar"],"max_batch_size":128,"dynamic_batching":true}'
```

They said toggling max_batch_size down to 32 reduced the error rate.

AJ (ML Eng): @Liz thanks — quick idea: looks like requests for different model variants (quantized 1024-dim vs full 1536-dim) are getting co-batched. Our dynamic-batching path used to partition by model_id+dim, but there was an optimization landed that relaxed partitioning to only model_id to improve fill rate. If a quantized variant was registered under the same model_id but with different output_dim we could mix them. That would explain dim mismatch errors and odd tail behavior when batches contain mixed variants because runtime tries to execute with a kernel configured for one dim.

Tori (Runtime): FYI I see a spike in cross-variant batching in the runtime logs around the time they reported issues. Snippet from runtime log: 
```
[2026-04-12T15:42:31Z] batch_builder: built batch id=0x7fef size=96 models=[embed-redwood-1@v2-q8_1024, embed-redwood-1@v1_full_1536]
[2026-04-12T15:42:31Z] dispatcher: dispatching kernel embed_kern_1024 for batch 0x7fef
[2026-04-12T15:42:31Z] exec: kernel failed: output_size_mismatch expected=1536 got=1024
[2026-04-12T15:42:31Z] request_id=xxx status=400 err="embedding dim mismatch"
```
So batches are indeed mixing variants. The p99 jump makes sense: when kernel fails we fallback to per-request serial handling which increases tail latency.

Liz (Support): That matches customer -> they said lowering max_batch_size made it less likely to mix variants. Is there a quick config we can push to avoid mixed-dim co-batching until we have a fix?

Tori (Runtime): We can flip a config flag to enforce stricter partitioning: batch_partition_key = model_id + output_dim. Right now the flag is off in hosted. Quick mitigation: set `allow_mixed_variant_batching=false` in the dynamic-batcher config for the affected pool. I can deploy that to the hosted pool serving embed-redwood-1 in region us-east-1. Will that break throughput too much for the customer?

AJ (ML Eng): That should prevent dim-mixing. Throughput might drop 5-15% at high QPS depending on distribution of variants, but it's acceptable for now. Longer-term we should:
- add runtime guard to reject / return 400 early for requests that explicitly request an incompatible variant via model_version or config
- add model registry metadata so variants with different dims are treated as separate model ids, or ensure quantized variants explicitly set output_dim in registration
- add unit tests preventing cross-dim co-batching

deploy-bot: Deploy queued by Tori: dynamic-batcher: enforce-partition-key-output-dim -> canary to hosted-us-east-1

metrics-bot: Chart: https://console.redwood.ai/metrics/embeddings/p99?from=2026-04-12T15:30&to=2026-04-12T16:00 (shows p99 drop after canary) :bar_chart:

Tori (Runtime): Canary applied. Early numbers look good: p99 for that pool dropped from ~1100ms to ~140ms within 6 minutes. Error rate for "dimension mismatch" went from 2.3% -> 0.02% for affected customer.

Liz (Support): Great. Customer also reported that sometimes requests succeed but embeddings have wrong dimension causing downstream code to crash. How do we prevent silent success?

AJ (ML Eng): Two things: (1) We should ensure the model registration advertises a strict output_dim and runtime refuses to accept requests that conflict (server-side validation). (2) Add shape metadata to the embeddings response header `x-embedding-dim: 1536` so clients can assert. We'll file a ticket to add that and push a short-term header patch.

Tori (Runtime): Filed RUNTIME-4567 for partition-key enforcement and RUNTIME-4568 for early validation. Also added a quick response header patch PR linked: https://git.redwood/patches/emb-dim-header diff. I'll follow up with the oncall to schedule a full regression test.

Liz (Support): For immediate customer-facing work:
- I will ask the customer to set `max_batch_size=32` or pin `model_version` to the full 1536 variant.
- Offer a credit for the interruptions.
- Confirm once the config change is live we will monitor for 24h.

Tori (Runtime): Confirmed config is live in us-east-1; will roll to other regions after monitoring.

AJ (ML Eng): FYI we should audit the catalog for models with multiple output dims under same model_id. I can run a quick query.

Liz (Support): Thanks all. I'll reply to customer with the workaround + ETA for full fix. Marking as in-progress and will update once customer confirms stability. :white_check_mark:

Tori (Runtime): Follow-up: added temporary guard in the batcher to drop mixed-dim candidates and route them to their own batches. Patch PR: https://git.redwood/patches/batcher-fix-789

Liz (Support): Customer confirmed after 3h that errors are gone and p99 improved. Closing on our side, leaving RUNTIME-4567 open for the full regression tests and model-catalog audit.

(End of thread)
